newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan spokesman lights fuse for SKorean summit.
newsitem.headline: Japan spokesman lights fuse for SKorean summit.

text.p: The Japanese media quoted the top government spokesman as saying on Friday, eve of a visit by South Korean President Kim Young-sam, that there was a "social background" to Tokyo's use of sex slaves during World War Two.

In remarks reported by Kyodo News Service which were likely to sour talks between Kim and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, he suggested only some of the sex slaves or so-called "comfort women" were forced into front-line prostitution.
The issue of the comfort women, which historians say involved hundreds of thousands of Filipino, Korean, Chinese and Indonesian women, is one of the key topics on the summit agenda.

"It is odd teaching them (Japanese schoolchildren) of the comfort women issue, without teaching the social background of an authorised prostitution system at that time," Chief Cabinet Secretary Seiroku Kajiyama Kajiyama, the top government spokesman, was quoted as telling Japanese reporters.

"Those who are making a fuss over the comfort women do not know that an authorised prostitution system existed in those days," he added. "When they (comfort women) went to the fronts, they got money. Among them, there were some who were drafted."

Hashimoto and Kim meet in the southern Japanese hot springs city of Beppu on Saturday afternoon to try to cool temperatures over comfort women and other issues of national pride which threaten bilateral relations.

The comfort women controversy, long a sore in Japan-Korea ties, flared again this month when South Korea denounced what it said was a Japanese government plan to avoid a national apology by using a private fund to compensate sex slaves for their suffering.

Under the scheme, a private Japanese group called the Asian Women's Fund, set up with heavy Japanese government support, offered to pay five million yen ($4,200) to each of seven ageing Koreans who were among nearly 200 registered comfort women.
Nine of at least 169 women in the Philippines have accepted a similiar offer of money along with a letter of apology from Hashimoto.
South Korea does not want government-to-government compensastion but believes Tokyo should compensate the sex slaves directly.
Other issues of national pride at stake in the summit are co-hosting of the 2002 World Cup, including where the soccer matches will be played, and who owns islands claimed by both nations.

The islands, called Takeshima by Japan and Tokto by South Korea, are surrounded by rich fishing grounds in the Sea of Japan. They make up an area of only 200 square metres (yards) about 420 miles west of Tokyo and 320 miles east of Seoul.

Tokyo has claimed the islands since 1905 under an treaty which paved the way for its colonial rule over the Korean peninsula until the end of World War Two in 1945. Korea says its claim to the islands dates back centuries.
